stem.en: A human cell has 46 chromosomes. Kabir says "so a sperm has 23 and an egg has 23, any 23 each". What is the constraint?

text.en: Twenty-three, and exactly one from each of the twenty-three pairs. Two from one pair and none from another would give a child with three of one chromosome and one of another, which mostly does not survive.

feedback.en: Half by count is not enough. It must be half by pairs, one of each, or genes go missing and double up.

text.en: Twenty-three, always the father's set or the mother's set whole.

feedback.en: Each pair separates on its own, so a gamete carries a mix of grandparents' chromosomes. That mix is the next lesson.

text.en: Forty-six, and the egg has none.

feedback.en: Both gametes carry twenty-three. Children get half from each parent, which is why they resemble both.

explanation.en: Meiosis separates pairs. Each gamete gets one member of every pair. The count halves and the set stays complete.
